chapter: Countess Johnson's band and the Kansas City scene
title: Personnel of the Countess Johnson group: Piggy Minor, Earl Jackson, Bill Nolan
summary: Piggy Minor, Earl Jackson, William Scott and Bill Nolan, several of whom went to McShann; Earl Jackson versus John Jackson.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We had Piggy Minor (phonetic) on trumpet, Earl Jackson --that's not John Jackson, now. Earl Jackson became before John Jackson, you know.

: Earl Jackson on the alto, and William Scott. We were all in Oliver Todd's band. And instead of usin' a drummer in Oliver Todd's band, we had a guy who would sing with the band sometime. That was Bill Nolan. And we put Countess on the thing--
: Bill Nolan -- he went with McShann too Chantue (phonetic), didn't he?
: Yeah, he came with McShann Max Hand's band later. And
: So, just let me get this again. Who was playing trumpet?
: Piggy Minor, Orville horrible (phonetic) "Piggy" Minor, the same one that--
: Isn't that funny? They both played the alto.
: They both play-ed the alto. In fact, one time Earl Jackson and John Jackson was in the band together, and then another time, John Jackson took Earl Jackson's place when he went away to college.
Well, now, what was Earl like? Was he a good alto player?
He was good. He would battle with Bird--I mean, but he was better than Bird, back in those days.
I mean, was he as good as Johns?
Yeah, well, in those days he was better than Johns. But he went away to college--but he didn't have that lead sound like what's-his-name.
